advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Emit an err/marker (not a silent return) when SELF_SNAPSHOT cannot be created so a failed self-update snapshot is observable instead of silently disabling the stale-body guard.
evidence: ABSENCE: no err/marker/log is emitted when SELF_SNAPSHOT ends up empty; a snapshot-acquisition failure is indistinguishable from a clean 'body unchanged' skip, so the very defect this guard protects against re-appears undetected.
ABSENCE: the `[ -f "$SELF_PATH" ]` false branch (script path missing after a sync) shares the silent return-0 path with the legitimate 'snapshot missing' case; no log distinguishes them.
advisory.finding: The self-update guard fails open silently when the snapshot cannot be taken: if mktemp fails or the cp of SELF_PATH fails, SELF_SNAPSHOT is set to empty, and reexec_if_self_changed's first guard `[ -n "$SELF_SNAPSHOT" ] && [ -f "$SELF_PATH" ] || return 0` returns 0 with no err/log. The same-tick stale-body bug (2d65-32dd-28b9-43ef) then recurs with zero diagnostic — the code cannot distinguish 'snapshot never taken' from 'body unchanged', and both silently skip the re-exec.
merged_from: reexec_if_self_changed also returns 0 silently when SELF_PATH no longer exists as a file (`[ -f "$SELF_PATH" ] || return 0`). A `rsync -a --delete` that removed/renamed the script's path (or a SELF_PATH resolved to a stale directory) would make the guard skip without any diagnostic, again masking a body change.
advisory.suggested_fix: When mktemp/cp fails, call `err self-snapshot-failed "could not snapshot running autodeploy.sh; same-tick body guard DISABLED for this tick"` (or abort the tick) rather than leaving SELF_SNAPSHOT empty and returning 0 silently.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update the MCP_PATHS mirror comment in infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:417 to include `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` so it matches the canonical value in infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:87.
evidence: infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:87: MCP_PATHS='src/rebar infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh infra/compose/docker-compose.yml uv.lock pyproject.toml'

infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:415-417 documents MCP_PATHS as 'the paths whose change should trigger an mcp blue-green redeploy' and enumerates the value as `MCP_PATHS="src/rebar infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh infra/compose/docker-compose.yml uv.lock pyproject.toml"`, which lacks the newly-added `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`

The comment is a developer-facing restatement of the canonical MCP_PATHS value; per docs/documentation-policy.md comments are corrected in place with the code (canonical source is the comment beside the relevant code)
advisory.finding: The MCP_PATHS trigger list changed in infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:87 to add `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`, but the maintained comment in infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:417 that restates the MCP_PATHS value verbatim still omits it (and `infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh`), so it no longer describes the current mcp blue-green redeploy triggers.
advisory.suggested_fix: In infra/compose/docker-compose.yml:417, update the quoted MCP_PATHS value to match autodeploy.sh:87, i.e. add `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` (and, if tracking exactly, `infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh`).

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that fires the bot-roll path (BOT_PATHS delta present) so reexec_if_self_changed at autodeploy.sh:784 is exercised, not only the mcp-roll seam at :855.
evidence: autodeploy.sh:784: `reexec_if_self_changed   # a body change to this script just landed on disk...` (bot-roll seam) is a distinct added call site from the mcp-roll one at :855

_GIT_STUB diff arm: `case "$*" in *Dockerfile.mcp*|*autodeploy.sh*) echo "infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp" ;; esac` — only ever reports the mcp-exclusive path, so `changed_range "$bot_deployed" "$TARGET" "$BOT_PATHS"` never matches and deploy_review_bot never runs

Named violating input: a commit whose only changed path is `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` on a box where BOT_PATHS matched (so the bot roll runs first) but the mcp delta does not — the line-784 re-exec is the only guard and no test drives it
autodeploy.sh:505-508: `if [ "$gen" -ge "$max" ]; then err self-update-reexec-capped ...; return 0; fi` — the loop hard-stop, newly added

AC3 test docstring: 'the re-exec neither double-rolls within a tick nor re-fires every tick' — asserts convergence (one roll across two ticks) but never forces the non-converging case that trips the cap

Named violating input: a mirror whose autodeploy.sh perpetually differs from the deploy copy after re-exec (rsync stub that keeps installing a distinct body each generation) — should reach `self-update-reexec-capped` and continue with the current body after exactly `max` re-execs, an untested path
blocking.finding: The bot-roll re-exec call site (autodeploy.sh:784) is never exercised by any test. The git stub reports only 'infra/compose/Dockerfile.mcp' as the changed range, so the bot deploy path (deploy_review_bot / the changed_range BOT_PATHS branch at line 828) never fires and reexec_if_self_changed at line 784 is never called. A regression that removed or mis-placed only the line-784 re-exec (leaving the mcp one intact) would pass the entire suite, yet the same stale-body defect the diff describes would recur for a body-only change that lands during a bot roll on a box where no mcp delta is present.
merged_from: The generation-cap hard stop (the explicit loop-prevention contract: `if [ "$gen" -ge "$max" ]` -> `err self-update-reexec-capped`, autodeploy.sh:505-508) has no test coverage. The commit message and code comment assert this is the 'hard stop should that invariant ever break', but every test converges via cmp -s after a single re-exec, so the cap branch never executes. AC3 ('no loop') verifies only the happy convergence path, not the bounded-generation backstop; a regression that broke the cap (e.g. never setting AUTODEPLOY_REEXEC_GEN, or an off-by-one on `max`) would not be caught.
blocking.suggested_fix: Add a test whose git stub reports a BOT_PATHS member (e.g. a src/rebar or review-bot source file) as the changed range and assert the re-exec runs the new body before the bot build, mirroring AC1 on the bot path.
